title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 89
paragraphs: The number of the triremes proved to be twelve hundred and seven, and these were the peoples who supplied them. The Phoenicians, together with the Syrians who live in Palestine, furnished three hundred; they were equipped thus: on their heads they wore leather caps very like the Greek kind, and they wore linen corselets and carried rimless shields and javelins. The Phoenicians, according to their own account, lived in ancient times by the Erythraean Sea, and from there passed over and now inhabit the coast of Syria. This part of Syria, all the way to Egypt, is called Palestine. The Egyptians furnished two hundred ships. On their heads they wore plaited helmets; they had hollow shields with wide rims and spears for sea-fighting, and great battle-axes. Most of them wore corselets and carried large knives.
